triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The branch selecting the higher $2,050 aged/blind additional amount was gated on a free, module-invented boolean input rather than on the taxpayer's filing status, so the encoding did not itself determine the source's condition ('unmarried and not a surviving spouse') and the higher amount could fire, or fail to fire, independently of the filing status the same module already uses for the basic deduction.
triage.triage_notes: Single-module commit; only one formula line changed (13 diff lines). Provision was read through the pinned corpus release (us/guidance/irs/rev-proc-2025-32/page-18): '.14 ... (3) Aged or blind. For taxable years beginning in 2026, the additional standard deduction amount under Sec. 63(f) for the aged or the blind is $1,650. The additional standard deduction amount is increased to $2,050 if the individual is also unmarried and not a surviving spouse.' The module's own enum (from rules[basic_standard_deduction_by_filing_status].versions[0].formula) is 1=joint, 4=surviving spouse, 3=head of household, 2=MFS, 0=unmarried, so the post-fix predicate (0 or 3) matches 'unmarried and not a surviving spouse' and excludes joint, MFS, and surviving spouse. Kind is a judgment call between untraceable_branch (chosen: the branch condition had no grounded derivation in the encoding and the fix re-grounds it on the filing-status table the source states) and 'other' (ungrounded free input for a derived legal classification); the classification 'fidelity' itself is well supported. Caveat a reviewer should weigh: the four companion test cases only lost the removed input line, no expected output changed, so the repair is behavior-preserving on the shipped tests and a reviewer could read it as structural rather than a wrong-answer defect. Corroborating mechanism read in axiom-encode src/axiom_encode/harness/validator_pipeline.py (find_tax_status_component_local_input_issues, ~line 23871): 'Tax filing-status component is a derived legal classification, not a local factual input'. The commit also touched non-module files (.axiom/encoding-manifests/.../standard-deduction.json re-signed under backend 'deterministic', tool 'axiom-encode repair-tax-status-components'; tests/test_repository_layout.py). Later commits 095d680d4 (refresh) and 86ec136fd (move under us/) did not revisit the predicate: the fix is still present at HEAD in us/policies/irs/rev-proc-2025-32/standard-deduction.yaml:281. PR #47 has no reviews or review comments.
triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as a mere modeling preference and could not: the pre-fix branch gating the higher aged/blind amount was an undefined, free boolean input (`individual_is_unmarried_and_not_surviving_spouse`) that no rule in the module defined and no import supplied, so the encoding did not itself determine the source's condition and could pay $2,050 to a joint filer or $1,650 to a single filer depending on an exogenous flag. The pinned corpus text ("The additional standard deduction amount is increased to $2,050 if the individual is also unmarried and not a surviving spouse.", us/guidance/irs/rev-proc-2025-32/page-18) ties the increase to the same marital/surviving-spouse status the module already encodes as `filing_status`, and the fix re-grounds the gate on that enum (0 unmarried, 3 head of household; excluding 1 joint, 2 MFS, 4 surviving spouse, which the module's own basic-deduction `match` and companion tests fix as the mapping), so the new predicate is itself faithful and the change is a correction rather than a lateral rewrite. This is not mechanical (a derived rule's formula and the module's input surface both changed), and the alternative kinds fit worse: no amount, boundary, date, or polarity changed, no source clause was added, and pre-fix there was no wrong population stated — only an ungrounded one — so untraceable_branch ("the fix removes or re-grounds it") is the right kind.

-          additional_standard_deduction_entitlement_count_under_subsection_f * (if individual_is_unmarried_and_not_surviving_spouse: additional_standard_deduction_amount_unmarried_not_surviving_spouse else: additional_standard_deduction_amount)
+          additional_standard_deduction_entitlement_count_under_subsection_f * (if filing_status == 0 or filing_status == 3: additional_standard_deduction_amount_unmarried_not_surviving_spouse else: additional_standard_deduction_amount)
triage.verifier_notes:
Evidence trail: bundle diff 000.diff (one formula line in rules[additional_standard_deduction_for_aged_or_blind].versions[0].formula); post file `git -C /Users/maxghenis/TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us show 5cdc45e555:policies/irs/rev-proc-2025-32/standard-deduction.yaml`; provision resolved through us-rulespec-2026-07-13 (corpus commit 612d20ca43, record 229d5117-ab80-57cd-973e-a0cd3f467b93).

Enum grounding is internal to the module and unambiguous: `basic_standard_deduction_by_filing_status` maps 1/4 => joint_or_surviving_spouse, 3 => head_of_household, 2 => married_filing_separately, 0 => unmarried, and the four companion test cases use 1 (joint), 3 (HoH), 0 (single dependent), 2 (MFS). So `filing_status == 0 or filing_status == 3` is exactly "unmarried and not a surviving spouse" (MFS filers are married, correctly excluded; test 4 expects 2 x 1650 = 3300).

Caveat a reviewer should weigh: the defect was latent under the committed tests. The companion test diff only deletes the now-unused `#input.individual_is_unmarried_and_not_surviving_spouse` lines; not a single expected output changed, because every test set the flag consistently with its filing_status. The behavioral divergence only appears on flag/filing-status combinations the source forbids, which is why this is "encoding does not determine the condition" rather than "encoding computes a wrong number".

Corroborating (tooling, not source): axiom-encode's own validator treats this exact pattern as an error — src/axiom_encode/harness/validator_pipeline.py:23871 `find_tax_status_component_local_input_issues`, message "Tax filing-status component is a derived legal classification, not a local factual input", and src/axiom_encode/prompts/encoder.py:1326 prohibits "compound status predicates such as `individual_is_not_married_and_is_not_surviving_spouse`" and prescribes the structural enum. That is repo-tooling evidence for the defect class, not source evidence; the source basis is the sentence quoted above.

No PR reviews or comments exist on rulespec-us#47, so the only narrative evidence is the PR body line the first reader quoted, which is verbatim and accurate.

Residual uncertainty (why 0.82, not higher): one could argue the module legitimately takes other status-ish facts as free inputs (`may_be_claimed_as_dependent_by_another_taxpayer`, `additional_standard_deduction_entitlement_count_under_subsection_f` remain free), so "free input" alone is not automatically a fidelity defect. The distinguishing fact I relied on is that this particular predicate was redundant with, and could contradict, a source-backed determinant already present in the same module.
